decisions.evidence: R1 maker spec required manual entry: client (R1) '#1 Typing in the title myself... I saw the note that I'd have to enter the title and details by hand. That's not really what I pictured... I'd expect the app to go grab the page's title and a short description for me automatically — and ideally the little site icon and a preview picture too'. Client also affirms edit: 'I still want to be able to fix or rewrite that title and description myself, both when saving and later'.
decisions.note: Spec-gate (prototype/spec review R1). Presented manual metadata entry diverges from REF-BM-02 (auto-collect title/description/favicon/preview). Client supplies the reference-conforming behaviour → correct. REF-BM-03 (edit before/after) is the conforming portion the client explicitly restated.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker presented 'duplicate warnings'; client (R1) '#2 Saving the same link twice. Your version warns me but lets me keep a second copy on purpose. I'd actually rather it never make duplicates — if I try to save a link I've already got, just take me to the one I already saved so I can edit it.'
decisions.note: Spec gate R1. Warn-and-allow-duplicate diverges from REF-BM-06 (converge to editing the existing bookmark). Client rejects the mismatch and supplies conforming behaviour → correct.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker scope had 'favoriting' but no read-later. Client (R1) '#3 Read later... I'd like to mark a bookmark as unread/to-read, and be able to look at just those in one place, then mark it read when I'm done so it drops off that list.'
decisions.note: Spec gate R1. Read-later/unread absent from presented scope. Client requests the missing reference requirements → extend (REF-BM-17/18/19).

decisions.evidence: R1 maker had delete only; client (R1) '#4 Archiving vs. deleting. Delete should be the permanent... action, yes. But I'd also like a gentler option — archive — to tuck a bookmark away so it's out of my normal list and searches but not actually destroyed, with its own place to look at archived ones and bring them back.'
decisions.note: Spec gate R1. Archive (reversible, hidden from list/search, separate archive list) absent from presented scope. Client requests missing reference requirements and distinguishes archive from delete → extend (REF-BM-26/27/28).

decisions.evidence: R1 maker presented notes (single-line); client (R1) '#5 Notes. I'd like the notes to be able to hold more than a line — a proper note I can format a bit and have it show nicely when I look at the bookmark.'
decisions.note: Spec gate R1. Presented note capability mismatches REF-BM-23 (markdown note rendered on view). Client supplies conforming behaviour (formatted, rendered) → correct.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker had plain-text search; client (R1) '#6 Searching... I'd also want to search by tag directly (something like typing the tag)'.
decisions.note: Spec gate R1. Tag search (#tag syntax) absent from presented scope → extend (REF-BM-14).

decisions.evidence: R1 client '#6 ...match an exact phrase when I put it in quotes'.
decisions.note: Spec gate R1. Quoted-phrase exact match absent from presented plain-text search → extend (REF-BM-16).

decisions.evidence: R1 client '#6 ...and combine conditions (this and that, or either one)'.
decisions.note: Spec gate R1. Boolean AND/OR combination absent from presented scope → extend (REF-BM-15).

decisions.evidence: R1 client '#6 ...And I'd like the tag box to suggest tags I've already used as I type.'
decisions.note: Spec gate R1. Tag autocomplete of existing tags absent from presented scope → extend (REF-BM-10).

decisions.evidence: R1 client '#7 Sorting. I don't only want newest-first — I'd like to choose how the list is ordered, like by title or by date.'; confirmed R2 maker default 'Sorting supports title, date added, and date updated in both directions'.
decisions.note: Spec gate R1. Presented newest-first-only ordering mismatches REF-BM-22 (sort by a chosen key). Client supplies conforming behaviour → correct.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker explicitly scoped out import/export: 'Current scope assumes a private, single-user app without... bulk import/export.' Client never mentions import/export in any round (R1–R5 reactions raise 7 other points and later approve).
decisions.note: Spec gate R1 — explicit exclusion decision. Diverges from REF-BM-30/31 (Netscape HTML import/export, extended items). Client neither corrected nor expressed the difference; passed without disposition → unexpressed_divergence.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker presented 'saving, editing, deleting, searching, tagging'; client (R1) 'a lot of it matches what I had in mind: saving links, editing them, deleting with a confirm, searching, tagging'.
decisions.note: Spec gate R1. Base features conform to REF-BM-01/04/05/09/12; recorded conforming decision, no divergence.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker documented default 'Similar URLs with different paths, queries, or fragments remain distinct.' Client (R2) 'Links that only look similar but go to different pages staying separate — that's right; I only want the truly-same link to be treated as a duplicate.'
decisions.note: Spec gate R2 refinement of the duplicate rule; conforms to REF-BM-06 edge case (only truly-same url is a duplicate). Recorded conforming decision — does not re-count the R1 corrective capture.
